Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1) demonstrates a large, homogeneous, well-circumscribed opacity that forms an obtuse angle with the chest wall, a classic radiographic sign indicating an extrapulmonary origin such as a pleural mass or loculated effusion rather than an intrapulmonary lesion. This is further supported by the axial CT images (Figures 2 and 3) which confirm a large, smooth-margined mass located in the pleural space.
